subject: Agriculture
title: Minerals in Soil
description: A fast breakdown of Minerals in Soil for builders.

hook.text: About 45% of soil is mineral matter—tiny fragments of the rocks that once towered above.

buildup.text: Quartz, feldspar, and mica are common soil minerals. Each weathers differently and contributes different nutrients.

discovery.text: Clay minerals are special—their tiny, flat plates have enormous surface area that holds nutrients and water.

twist.text: Not all clays are equal. Montmorillonite swells when wet and cracks when dry. Kaolinite stays stable.

climax.text: The mineral mix determines what a soil can grow. Farmers can add nutrients, but can't change the minerals.

punchline.text: Every field is built on the bones of ancient mountains.

quiz.question: Why are clay minerals important in soil?
options: Their large surface area holds nutrients and water

details.summary: Soil minerals make up about 45% of soil volume and provide the essential nutrients plants need to grow. This topic covers primary minerals inherited from parent rock, secondary minerals formed by weathering, and the sixteen essential plant nutrients supplied by soil minerals.
details.whyItMatters: Mineral composition determines soil fertility, pH, and structure. The sixteen essential elements plants extract from soil minerals are the foundation of crop nutrition, and their availability drives fertilizer decisions worldwide.
takeaways: Minerals make up roughly 45% of soil volume and provide essential plant nutrients
Primary minerals like quartz and feldspar weather into secondary clay minerals
Plants require sixteen essential mineral nutrients, with nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium most critical

faq.question: What are the most important minerals found in agricultural soil?
faq.answer: Quartz provides soil structure. Feldspar and mica weather to release potassium, calcium, and magnesium. Clay minerals (kaolinite, montmorillonite) hold water and nutrients. Iron and aluminum oxides affect soil color and phosphorus availability. Calcite buffers soil pH.

faq.question: Which mineral nutrients do crops need most from soil?
faq.answer: The primary macronutrients are nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (NPK). Secondary macronutrients include calcium, magnesium, and sulfur. Micronutrients like iron, zinc, manganese, and boron are needed in small quantities but are equally essential for plant health.
